summary: Sweden does not record ethnicity. Brå's school survey gives grade-9 pupils' experience of sexual offences and assault by migration background, and a one-off 2021 study gave suspects of sexual offences, assault and lethal violence by background with rates for 2015-2018. No regular statistics give the background of child victims or offenders; neglect, trafficking and online abuse have none.

european_title: Not recorded by any Swedish source
european_note: Swedish statistics describe background by country of birth of the person and their parents, never ethnicity. 'Born in Sweden to two Swedish-born parents' is the closest group to ethnic Europeans but is a birth-country proxy: it includes people of any descent, and people born abroad include Europeans and non-Europeans.
proxy_note: Sweden records background by country of birth of the person and parents, never ethnicity. Every group below is a proxy, not ethnicity.

harms.label: Sexual offences
harms.intro: No regular statistics give the background of child victims or offenders. Brå's school survey shows how many grade-9 pupils were subjected to sexual offences by migration background (2025), and a one-off Brå study gave people suspected of sexual offences in 2015-2018 by background, for victims of all ages.

victims.scope: Sweden, grade-9 pupils (about age 15), national school survey, 2025
victims.rate_label: of grade-9 pupils in the group said they had been subjected to a sexual offence in the past 12 months
victims.share_note: Official Brå survey (Skolundersökningen om brott), every two years. Self-reported; age 15 only. Brå combines pupils born in Sweden with one or two Swedish-born parents into one group. Background by country of birth of the person and their parents (inrikes/utrikes bakgrund), a proxy, not ethnicity: Swedish statistics never record ethnicity, and 'born in Sweden to two Swedish-born parents' includes people of any descent.

breakdown.why: Brå's 2025 school survey gives the share of grade-9 pupils subjected to a sexual offence by migration background (10.8% Swedish-born with a Swedish-born parent, 11.5% foreign-born); age 15 only. Brå's one-off 2021 study gives suspects of sexual offences 2015-2018 by background with rates per 1,000, all victims.
The same school survey gives assault victimization by background (18.8% vs 21.7%); the 2021 study gives assault suspects by background with rates, all victims, 2015-2018.
No national neglect statistics by any origin variable were found.

Brå's confirmed lethal violence statistics give 4 child victims in 2025 with no background. The 2021 study gives suspects of lethal violence (including attempts) by background with rates, all victims, 2015-2018.

The Police situation report for 2024 gives 430 identified victims (22 children) and only a ranked list of origin countries (Thailand, Ukraine, Romania, Sweden, ...), with no counts and no suspect nationality.
No statistics on online child sexual exploitation by any origin variable were found.

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify ethnic European children (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump ethnic Europeans with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, ethnic Europeans separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies ethnic Europeans, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when ethnic European children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points (victims 37.5, perpetrators 37.5); coverage, rates and access share the other 25. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points. A country with no real ethnicity data for victims or perpetrators is capped at 25%.
score.why: Sweden scores 13% on the stricter scale (0-20%). Brå's school survey shows grade-9 pupils' experience of sexual offences and assault by migration background, and a one-off 2021 study gave suspects by background with rates for 2015-2018. No regular statistics give the origin of child victims or offenders, and neglect, online abuse and trafficking have almost none.
score.weights_id: harm weights of 19 Nov 2026 (homicide 25, sexual abuse 20, sex trafficking 20, physical abuse 15, online exploitation 10, neglect 10)

availability_note: Each harm has an 'availability' map listing the victim and perpetrator groups with any published figure (overall and by measure) and any linked victim-perpetrator pairs. Groups not listed have no data for that harm; the explorer should grey them out rather than offer an empty combination.
